claims.objects: The smooth nonstandard A5-invariant pencil of cubic threefolds and its projective-line stabilization.
claims.hypotheses: A complex point of the connected smooth locus of the pencil.
claims.conclusion: Universal CH0-triviality of the fibre and its stabilization, irrationality of the stabilization, and non-isotriviality of the family.
claims.cautions: The cycle argument is fibrewise and the irrationality argument applies more broadly than the A5-family.

claims.objects: An abstract geometric signature naming smooth complex cubic threefolds, product with projective one-space, projective four-space, and rationality, together with a natural-valued packet multiplicity.
claims.hypotheses: The carrier satisfies the smooth-cubic predicate, its packet equals two, the named product obeys the rank-two formula and dimension bound, projective four-space has zero packet, and rationality supplies the required birational relation.
claims.conclusion: The named product of the specified cubic carrier with projective one-space is not rational.
claims.cautions: The geometric signature and every quantum, weak-factorization, and rational-comparison fact remain typed premises rather than foundational constructions.

claims.objects: The six elliptic quotient axes of the intermediate Jacobian and their Rosati pairing.
claims.hypotheses: A smooth member of the nonstandard A5-pencil with coherent elliptic-factor identifications.
claims.conclusion: Rosati Gram matrix 6I-J and five-axis Smith type (1,6,6,6,6).
claims.cautions: The coherent identification and non-CM generic-fibre passage are part of the human proof.

claims.objects: The relative elliptic scheme, augmentation-lattice source, intermediate-Jacobian family, and relative isogeny.
claims.hypotheses: The connected smooth locus of the nonstandard A5-pencil.
claims.conclusion: An A5-equivariant polarized relative isogeny and its two-primary symplectic discriminant description.
claims.cautions: Primitivity, finite flatness, and generic-to-relative transport must be represented explicitly.

claims.objects: A5-stable maximal isotropic kernels in the two- and three-primary discriminant modules.
claims.hypotheses: The relative six-axis source and its polarized A5-action.
claims.conclusion: The P1(F4) packet, stabilizers and outer exchange at two, exotic geometric selection, and scalar graphs at three.
claims.cautions: The family-level exotic selection uses Torelli, connectedness, and the generic automorphism group.

claims.objects: A marked finite-etale graph presentation over a complete unramified DVR and its descended symmetric coefficient lattice.
claims.hypotheses: Depth decomposition, dual-form adjointness, and finite-etale slope algebra on every positive-depth summand.
claims.conclusion: The exact diagonal and cross-ideal depths and the midpoint inequality.
claims.cautions: No etaleness is imposed on the unit block and scalar lifts must not affect the depth formula.

claims.objects: Lean currently represents only three coefficients of a symmetric form over a commutative ring.
claims.hypotheses: Three arbitrary ring elements; no DVR, valuation, ideals, or lattice-membership hypotheses are formalized.
claims.conclusion: The midpoint inequality supplies parity-compatible exponents, and every multiple of the cross generator has the division-free three-rank-one coefficient decomposition.
claims.cautions: The DVR lattice-membership proof, necessity, assembly over all matrix entries, and rank-one generation conclusion are absent.

claims.objects: The prescribed graph divisor lattice and its divided-power and ordinary product images.
claims.hypotheses: A marked finite-etale graph presentation over the localized coefficient ring.
claims.conclusion: Equality of the divided-power envelope and ordinary divisor-product image in every degree.
claims.cautions: The result is cohomological, concerns only the prescribed graph lattice, and does not assert a Chow divided-power statement.

claims.objects: The lattice with Gram matrix 6I5-J5 at primes two and three and the principal quotient graph slope.
claims.hypotheses: The actual six-axis geometric kernels selected by the gluing packet.
claims.conclusion: A unit line plus a depth-one rank-four block, with quadratic finite-etale slope at two and scalar slope at three.
claims.cautions: Persistence through the connected smooth component and identification of the actual kernel are essential.

claims.objects: The six-axis graph divisor lattice on the intermediate Jacobian of each smooth A5-pencil member.
claims.hypotheses: The local charts at two and three, trivial integral comparison elsewhere, and finite generation of the cokernels.
claims.conclusion: All integral divided powers lie in the ordinary product image, in particular Theta^4/4!.
claims.cautions: Extra Neron-Severi classes at special fibres only enlarge the target product image.

claims.objects: A smooth cubic threefold in the nonstandard A5-pencil and its intermediate Jacobian.
claims.hypotheses: Algebraicity of the primitive minimal class and the exact Voisin criterion.
claims.conclusion: Universal CH0-triviality of the cubic threefold.
claims.cautions: The proof is fibrewise and constructs neither a horizontal cycle nor a relative decomposition of the diagonal.

claims.objects: Framed formal monodromy of the numerical small even quantum connection.
claims.hypotheses: A smooth projective complex variety and the original unramified loop coordinate z.
claims.conclusion: The sum of the algebraic multiplicities of the two primitive sixth-root eigenvalues.
claims.cautions: Adjoining roots of z is forbidden because it changes the frame and may erase deck monodromy.

claims.objects: A compatible system of differential modules over finite quotients of a complete filtered coefficient algebra.
claims.hypotheses: Agreement of the finite-level characteristic polynomials and gauges using only integral powers of z.
claims.conclusion: A well-defined pro-Laurent framed-monodromy characteristic polynomial.
claims.cautions: The pro-Laurent gauge group may be larger than matrices with one uniform Laurent lower bound.

claims.objects: A formal differential module and coefficientwise extension to a complete separated adic algebra.
claims.hypotheses: The coefficient algebra is constant for d/dz; any gauge uses integral powers of z.
claims.conclusion: Preservation of the framed-monodromy characteristic polynomial.
claims.cautions: The assertion is coefficientwise and does not authorize ramification of the loop coordinate.

claims.objects: A bulk pullback of the even quantum connection over a complete multiplicatively filtered ring.
claims.hypotheses: The unit and fixed divisor components are constant in positive filtration and the remainder is filtration-positive.
claims.conclusion: Equality with the small-connection characteristic polynomial after the stated divisor substitution.
claims.cautions: Only finite-quotient integral-z gauges are used; no analytic specialization or enlarged Levelt-Turrittin field is asserted.

claims.objects: Completed effective homology and numerical Novikov monoid rings and the relevant quantum connections.
claims.hypotheses: Degree filtrations with finite bounded pieces and comparison maps defined over the homological rings.
claims.conclusion: Continuous numerical quotient and base change of the quantum connection and comparison theorems.
claims.cautions: Continuity and inverse-limit compatibility are part of the claim.

claims.objects: Projective bundles and blowups of smooth projective varieties together with framed packet multiplicities.
claims.hypotheses: Rank and codimension bounds, Iritani comparison coordinates, and the displayed numerical specializations.
claims.conclusion: The rank-multiplication projective-bundle formula and additive blowup formula.
claims.cautions: Center terms are specialized invariants; endpoint terms remain intrinsic and loop-coordinate roots are not adjoined.

claims.objects: A monomial map from a numerical Novikov ring to a complete separated valued domain.
claims.hypotheses: Nonzero monomial images, a positive proper valuation law, and domain associated graded.
claims.conclusion: The predicate of strict Novikov admissibility.
claims.cautions: Properness and the domain hypothesis are used to prevent cancellation in the divisor-tagging argument.

claims.objects: The intrinsic and specialized small even quantum connections under a strictly admissible monomial map.
claims.hypotheses: Intrinsic absence of primitive-sixth framed monodromy and strict Novikov admissibility.
claims.conclusion: Absence persists after specialization.
claims.cautions: Generic vanishing alone is insufficient without divisor tags because the center map may be noninjective.

claims.objects: Points, smooth projective curves, and smooth projective surfaces with specialized framed multiplicity.
claims.hypotheses: Every strictly Novikov-admissible specialization.
claims.conclusion: Vanishing of the primitive-sixth multiplicity.
claims.cautions: The proof separates nef-canonical minimal models, projective and ruled cases, and point blowups.

claims.objects: An arbitrary carrier type with a natural-valued multiplicity, dimension function, arbitrary birational relation, and preserving chains.
claims.hypotheses: A dimension bound and a bundled premise producing a preserving chain for the chosen relation.
claims.conclusion: Equality of multiplicities at the endpoints of that abstract chain.
claims.cautions: Smoothness, projectivity, complex structure, equal dimension, blowups, centers, operation formulas, and weak factorization are not formalized.

claims.objects: The numerical small even quantum connection of a smooth complex cubic threefold.
claims.hypotheses: Cai's integral-z block diagonalization and the numerical-Novikov convention.
claims.conclusion: Primitive-sixth framed multiplicity exactly two.
claims.cautions: The two rank-one blocks and the rank-two indicial polynomial must both be accounted for.

claims.objects: An abstract geometric signature naming smooth prime genus-eight Fano threefolds, their associated Pfaffian cubics, both rank-two projective-bundle total spaces, product with projective one-space, projective four-space, and rationality.
claims.hypotheses: The specified carrier satisfies the genus-eight predicate, its associated cubic satisfies the smooth-cubic predicate, both named total spaces obey the rank-two formulas and are birational, the cubic packet is two, and the named stabilization and rational comparison have the stated properties.
claims.conclusion: The specified Fano carrier has packet multiplicity two and its named product with projective one-space is irrational.
claims.cautions: The geometric signature and the Kuznetsov, quantum, weak-factorization, and rational-comparison facts remain typed premises rather than foundational constructions.
